So after 150+ hours, I finally came to my conclusion that this game just lacks any long term value it can provide.

I just don't know what else I can do in this game to enjoy it. You can't really PVP, withour grinding gear like a maniac. You can't rellay do PVE, because some toxic dudes will just ambush you whenever you are trying to do something fun, like kill the queen.

Then I watch streamers play this game and realize, their experience of the game is completely different than probably most others. I see Shroud's stream, where people are super friendly to him, once they realize it's  a gaming celebrity. Well, I and mostly any other player never gets this treatment. I have never been revived by an enemy before, not once.

Then there is are the teams these streamers go in with. Mostly high skilled players, since they do it professionally. Of course they are going to rock, have the best gear, get treated like royalty and then tout how awesome this game is. It's not the same experience for the average player. 

I feel like this game was made for streamers, and streamers alone. You will get awesome visuals, amazing sound effects, mostly good maps and still enjoy the game for a few hours. For 40EUR totally recommended to still buy and play it.

But the longterm value dropped drastically for me. Now I am mostly just wandering aroung the map, not really knowing what to do. With a free loadout, you only have a chance vs. other player with a free loadout. If you are fighting against an enemy that has just basic gear, all other things being equal, he will devestate you. The difference between a level 1 weapon compared to a level 3 or 4 weapon is just completely senseless. It's like you have a completely different weapon.

I didn't want to rant for that long, but somehow my disappointment is so big, that I needed to let of some steam. Because this game has great potential, but it chose to make it as unpleasant as it can for most players. I know some streamers are pretending this game is so awesome, but also they are mostly just wandering around the map looking for some kind of action. And if you disagree with their hype, they will tell you that you don't get it or that's just how it is.

I strongly disagree. Embark created an amazing world, pretty cool gameplay and lots of other good things. But then it fails at delivering a longterm gaming experience. Once I finished all the quests, built my project, found most of the Blueprints I wanted, it just left me behind feeling empty. 

Maybe I revisit this after a while, when there is something more clear to do in the game. But for now, if you are looking for a new alternative to something like CoD Warzone or Battlefield, this game will not deliver in the longterm. You can't just hop on and enjoy it for a couple hours a day. People will say. "well, it's  an extraction shooter". Well, does it have to be? Why do we have to just accept, that the boring parts about extraction shooters have to remain the same. Battle Royale evolved, so should extraction shooters? Maybe?

STILL: For 40EUR I think you should still give it a go just to see, what a Game in 2025 should technically look like. They made good use of the Unreal Engine and it really is an experience to see the possibilities, once you let the Devs just work. Hopefully, they can introduce new ideas that also ensures the joy of playing this game for more than 100 hours.

I am a 44 year old father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my son, who is now 14. My son recently started this game and in less than a week, he had already played for over 20 hours. This was terrible for me, as it was already hard enough for me to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching videos on Tiktok. So I decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, did the tutorial but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought my son and I closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

Any game that feels the need to include a voice changer in the settings is a "boy game" - you know what I mean. But against all odds, I have persevered and I am having the time of my life. Arc Raiders is visually stunning. I'm pretty sure the sound is magic. I haven't killed any raiders yet, but the time will come. I will cry when it does, and then everything will be okay. My favourite thing about this game is that it is so compelling and anxiety-inducing that I don't feel the need to have any other forms of entertainment in the background. Typically when I play games I throw on some music or a movie, but with Arc Raiders, I am so invested in not dying that I can't have any distractions or background noise. If you have any reservations about this game, don't. It's a hoot and a half!!

It's my 100th Steam Review, and I can't think of a more deserving title.

[i]ARC Raiders[/i] is probably the most pure distillation of the [b]"prisoner's dilemma simulator"[/b] concept in contemporary extraction shooters. Compared to [i]Tarkov[/i] or [i]Arena Breakout[/i], the NPC enemy AI is very erratic and dangerous and -- at the higher end -- basically insurmountable for a solo player to take on without teaming up with others or getting third-partied.  Compared to [i]Hunt: Showdown[/i], where the singular objective of the boss token puts all players into direct conflict, the idea of competing for generic resources is more abstract.  The local voice chat and canned voice prompts are similarly geared towards communication and collaboration.  But also, you're keenly aware at all times that if you enter that looting animation to check a closet, any cool chatty Raider you come across can and will just magdump into your back and freely get anything you're carrying.  [i]ARC Raiders[/i] cultivates a friendlier atmosphere than other extraction shooters, but with that friendliness comes a constant, uneasy paranoia where it always feels like a coin flip if a collaboration will end in betrayal.

This generates a rich depth of ambiguous player interactions that I can sum up using the most fun solo run I've had as an example:

> Spawn into Dam Battleground at the red lake
> Use the canned [b]"Greet"[/b] response on another nearby solo, causing him to spray a few shots in my direction, panic and run away
> Don't sweat it, walk past testing annex, giving it a wide berth because somebody's aggro'd an ARC Rocketeer and that ♥♥♥♥ will kill you dead
> Head to scrapyard, where I have to do a quest
> Guy pops out of the rubble and aims his gun, demanding, [b]"Friendly? Friendly?"[/b]
> I respond [b]"yeah, I'm just doing the scrapyard quest"[/b] over voice comms
> We both interact with the quest items and silently go our separate ways
> I start heading for center extract because I have to bring out three items from the scrapyard quest and I don't want to do the whole rigmarole all over again
> A Ferro shot lands at my feet with a BANG and I hear a distant voicechat announce, [b]"THAT ONE WAS A WARNING!  I'M EXTRACTING HERE.  WALK AWAY."[/b]
> Don't want to fight a Ferro uphill, so I voicechat back [b]"okay, I'll go annex"[/b] and double back to the annex
> That guy trying to fight the Rocketeer is having a bad time of it.  See the 'zap' of it popping his shield when it plonks a rocket into the annex building
> See another dude with a Toro go sprinting into the building
> Smell a rat, make to follow
> Hear the 'BOOM' as he murders the guy fighting the Rocketeer while the poor dude is healing
> Round the corner and magdump my Rattler into him as he tries to loot the corpse, yelling [b]"I SAW WHAT YOU DID, YOU MURDERER!  GUARDS!  GUARDS!"[/b]
> A full mag of Rattler does 90 damage.  He has 100 health.  Thankfully for me he doesn't realize I have to reload and freaks out and starts running through the building on his last health
> I sprint after him, reloading as I run and yelling [b]"GUARDS!  THIS MAN IS A MURDERER!  GUARDS!"[/b]
> He stops to shoot an ARC Pop that aggro'd and was about to cherry-tap him, giving me the opening to put four more freshly-reloaded bullets into his back and drop him
> Beat him to death with my crowbar while going [b]"Nyeh!  Hahhh!  Have at you, fiend!"[/b]
> Loot both him and his victim, pack my bags full of Tier IV guns that both of them had in both slots
> Trundle down to annex extract and get shot in the back by an extract camper who's been bush wookieing all game
> [i]Another[/i] guy rounds the corner, mows down my killer with a Burletta before he can finish me, and then calls the extract elevator for me before saying [b]"I saw what you did up there, that was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious."[/b]
> He doesn't finish me off and we extract together with my backpack full of guns while I'm in bleedout

The game started off with players teaming up to take on bots. I’ve come over from Helldivers so this was great. The added risk of losing all your loot made it crazy tense and the joy of extracting with a full inventory was a delight.  Now it’s just a pvp arena where everyone shoots 1st out of fear if not pure aggression. Even when you focus on the bots there’s always a team of guys waiting to ambush you while you’re tussling with a mechanical menace. The amount of times my team has been picked off while we’ve been minding our own business killing bots is ridiculous. It seems like players are also happy to just camp corners and wait for someone to come. Boring. Not fun for anyone surely? … the game needs a PvE only area or that shiny player count will plummet in weeks. I for one will be heading back to Super Earth. For liberty, for freedom, for … fun.

This is not a PvP game, and PvP isn't (and should not) ever be a primary factor! The main threat is the PvE, PvP adds a dynamic element. My personal experience so far is that the majority of the players I've run into are peaceful and will help out. 

Proximity chat and quick emotes help to spread the friendly and non-PvP intentions (of course, not everyone is honest - but that's the risk factor) and bringing down huge enemies with a rag tag bunch that stumbled across the battle is such a rewarding factor.

I was initially unsure about this game as I dislike PvP (I'm a casual dad gamer) and sure, in my first couple of runs I almost refunded because PvP was ruining it for me; but then I had some great runs, ran into friendly raiders, helped each other and PvE became the dominant theme. At 40+ hours I've had almost 100 safe extractions, maybe 5 runs killed by PvP, and probably 20 runs killed by PvE/environment.

This is quickly becoming my main game and I just can't wait to get back in game.

Best extraction shooter available right now, by a long shot. Greatly improved the mechanics and gameplay features of all previous games in the genre. This is the new standard bearer for extraction shooters and what most players will expect in terms of features and quality for future competitors.

Edit: At the time of my original review, Marathon had yet to release. Now, as things stand, Marathon is clearly the superior game in every way and by more than a mile. It surpassed Arc Raiders easily in terms of quality, depth, story, gunplay and features. At this point, everything I said in my original review no longer stands true. However, I still love and play Arc Raiders constantly as it remains a fantastic, high quality game, which is also very fun to play and quite relaxing.
